headline: Lindbergh crossed the Atlantic alone in May, Al Jolson spoke from a screen in October, and Ruth hit sixty
texture: Charles Lindbergh flew from New York to Paris alone and without stopping on May 20 and 21, and came back to a level of fame no pilot had known. Babe Ruth hit sixty home runs, a major league record, and the Yankees took the World Series in four games. Nicola Sacco and Bartolomeo Vanzetti were electrocuted at midnight in Charlestown after seven years of appeals, and protests were held across the world.

The Jazz Singer premiered at the Warner Theater in New York on October 6 with Al Jolson speaking and singing in synchronised sound. It finished second for the year at $1,974,000 in rentals, behind Cecil B. DeMille's The King of Kings. Every studio spent the following months working out what to do about it.

Philo Farnsworth got a fully electronic television system working on September 7, and in April Bell Telephone had transmitted a picture of Herbert Hoover over a wire. Carving began at Mount Rushmore on October 4, four months after Coolidge rededicated the park. None of the television work reached a single home this year, or for years after.

notes: Research pass July 2026. No prices section: the three price series all start later. No awards section: the first Academy Awards ceremony was not held until 1929, which is where the film.awards window opens, so the films of this year were honoured on a page two years ahead. The Sacco and Vanzetti fact carries no date because the source sentence begins after it, and August 23 from memory is not good enough. Isadora Duncan died this year but appears in the source as an undated sub-entry, so she is left out.
